mechanism_narrative: PARKS has fallen monotonically from -17.4 to -24.1 over the last three weeks as mid-summer heat suppresses outdoor trips. Because park visits and discretionary retail trips share the same leisure-trip budget, the loss of outdoor activity drains total out-of-home excursion volume and drags RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declines 2.2 points per week on average across t-3w..t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or above its last-28-day mean while PARKS keeps declining by at least 2 points per week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the most normalized category, recovering from -5.0 to -2.4 before a one-week dip to -3.7. A re-crossing above -3.0 means households have restored routine errand trips; restored errand routines generalize to adjacent non-essential retail within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean holds above -3.0 for two consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is below its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Commuter-linked retail demand requires TRANSIT and WORKPLACES to recover jointly because transit delivers the footfall and workplaces supply the daytime population. Both series have stalled (TRANSIT -30.4, WORKPLACES -20.4 for three straight weeks), so the joint-recovery term is absent and RETAIL_REC cannot rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves by less than 1 point week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -25
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -20.4 across t-2w, t-1w, t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT stays below -25 and WORKPLACES stays flat.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has been pinned at 10.9-11.1 for four weeks, indicating that stay-at-home policy intensity has stopped relaxing. A frozen residential-anchoring regime caps the population available for discretionary store visits, so RETAIL_REC stays flat-to-lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above 10.5 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL values 11.1, 10.9, 10.9, 10.9 show a four-week plateau
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is above its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 10.5 for every week of the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS dropping below -22 in mid-July marks heat-driven substitution away from outdoor activity into climate-controlled indoor venues such as malls and restaurants. This substitution pushes RETAIL_REC up within one week of the parks threshold being crossed.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crosses -22 for the first time at t-0w (-24.1)
regime_hint: mid-summer heat wave under steady restrictions
failure_condition: In the week after PARKS sits below -22.0, RETAIL_REC prints at or below its t-0w value of -27.0.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES improved from -22.4 to -20.4 but then stopped moving for two consecutive weeks. A workplace-recovery stall means the reopening impulse that refills commercial districts has been exhausted; without new daytime population, RETAIL_REC loses its incremental lift and drifts lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean changes by less than 0.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reads -20.7, -20.4, -20.4 across the last three weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES remains within 0.5 points week-on-week yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Trip-chaining returns only when normalized grocery errands and a non-deteriorating transit system coincide: GROCERY_PHARM above -4.0 supplies the anchor errand and TRANSIT above -32.0 supplies the ability to reach it. Both conditions currently hold jointly, so chained trips into adjacent retail lift RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean above -4.0 and TRANSIT weekly mean above -32.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM above -4.0 and TRANSIT above -32.0 in every one of the last four weeks
regime_hint: partial reopening with transit service intact
failure_condition: Both trigger conditions hold for two consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under a home-anchored regime, high RESIDENTIAL combined with a RETAIL_REC reading stuck near -27 shows households are not converting home time into local retail spend. The combination of residential anchoring and retail stagnation predicts continued RETAIL_REC weakness over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL at or above 10.5 and RETAIL_REC within 1 point of -27.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC spans only -25.7 to -27.6 across all four weeks
regime_hint: home-anchored restrictions with retail demand suppressed
failure_condition: The trigger holds for two consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is above its last-28-day mean.
